active_paradigms.idea: Use memoized exact cardinality-constrained subset DP for the final GPU packing on small node-local instances
active_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns fixed logical groups to nodes, greedily adds replicas within each node, and then uses LPT to place equal-count physical experts on GPUs. Its one swap considers only the single current heaviest and lightest GPU pack, so it can miss a repartition in which several non-extreme bins must change simultaneously. Replace the final `balanced_packing(tokens_per_phy, gpus_per_node)` only when its instance is small enough with an exact feasibility DP: for a candidate makespan T, enumerate capacity-`phy_experts_per_gpu` subsets whose summed replica load is at most T, and recursively cover the remaining replicas with the remaining GPUs. Cache states keyed by the remaining-item bitmask and number of packs, using `functools.lru_cache`; binary-search only among attainable subset sums or retain the best completed partition during the recursion. This directly optimizes the quantity that the final placement controls: maximum per-GPU replica-token load, rather than the current LPT surrogate plus one exchange. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking by trying subsets in lexicographic physical-expert order and write the selected subset order into `pack_index` and `rank_in_pack`. Use this exact path only below a strict combinatorial threshold and retain the present LPT path above it, so the evaluator's runtime component cannot be harmed on large configurations.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The post-replication per-GPU bottleneck, which is the last opportunity to reduce load imbalance without changing replica counts or violating node locality; use it selectively so combined score does not lose runtime performance.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not use a generic MILP or flow formulation, since those have already shown no gain and add setup overhead. Every GPU must receive exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` physical experts, including low-load and zero-load replicas. DP states must use integer indices/bitmasks rather than floating-point loads; compare floating sums with a small tolerance only in feasibility tests. Set a hard instance-size cutoff based on number of local physical experts, because unrestricted subset enumeration is exponential.

active_paradigms.idea: Use branch-and-bound enumeration of replica-count vectors jointly with the node bottleneck bound
active_paradigms.description: The current `replicate_experts` greedily replicates the logical expert with largest individual value `weight/logcnt` independently inside each already selected node. That rule is optimal only for minimizing the largest individual replica share; it ignores that replicas must subsequently be packed in fixed-count GPU bins, and it cannot trade a slightly larger individual share for a much better packable multiset. For each layer-node instance with a manageable redundancy budget, enumerate feasible allocations of the redundant copies among its local logical experts using `itertools.combinations_with_replacement`, interpreting an emitted multiset as experts receiving one additional replica. Score each complete count vector by constructing its replica loads and applying a fast lower bound `max(max_replica_load, total_load/num_local_gpus)` plus a deterministic greedy upper bound. Prune count vectors whose lower bound cannot beat the incumbent, and retain the count vector whose actual capacity-constrained GPU packing has the smallest maximum load. This is fundamentally a replica-allocation search, not a replacement for the failed flow, MILP, or water-filling approaches, and it attacks the coupling that the existing sequential hierarchy leaves unresolved. Restrict it to small redundancy counts and fall back exactly to the existing greedy replication when the combination count exceeds a fixed budget.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Joint replica-count and GPU-packability quality, especially workloads where a few hot experts receive many copies and greedy marginal replication leaves awkward medium-load replicas that dominate one GPU.
active_paradigms.cautions: The enumeration must allocate exactly `num_physical_experts/num_nodes - num_logical_experts/num_nodes` redundant slots and must maintain `phyrank` as contiguous ranks 0 through count-1 for each logical expert. Do not score count vectors solely by `max(weight/count)`: the selected objective must include the fixed-experts-per-GPU packing constraint. Bound enumeration before materializing all combinations, otherwise layers with large redundancy budgets will time out. Keep all choices layer-local because the returned maps and observed load metrics are layer-local.

active_paradigms.idea: Use TorchScript specialization to reduce evaluator-time overhead while preserving the successful hierarchy
active_paradigms.description: The current result benefits from a sound cheap hierarchy: group sums limit cross-node traffic, marginal greedy replication reduces dominant expert load, and LPT plus one inward swap cheaply improves bin range. Its main execution-cost weakness is Python-level work for every layer and every packing call: `.tolist()`, Python heaps, nested swap loops, and repeated small tensor construction force synchronization and interpreter dispatch. Keep the same mapping semantics but implement the common bounded-shape packing kernel with tensor loops and compile that kernel once with `torch.jit.script`; use integer occupancy, tensorized masked argmin for selecting non-full lightest packs, and tensor reductions for the optional refinement. This is not a change in the optimization objective, so it is low risk to mapping validity, but it can improve the combined score if the original evaluator includes execution time as the prompt indicates. The scripted kernel should preserve the current deterministic tie rule by choosing the lowest pack index among equal loads and use float32 exactly as the entry point does. Retain the existing Python implementation as a fallback for dynamic shapes or unsupported TorchScript constructs, and avoid compiling repeatedly per invocation.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time and score consistency, while retaining the current hierarchy, greedy replication policy, and valid `phy2log`/`phyrank` mapping behavior that already produce the baseline balance score.
active_paradigms.cautions: Compilation startup can exceed the savings if the evaluator imports and calls the candidate only once; cache the scripted function at module scope and benchmark the actual fresh-process evaluator before adopting it. TorchScript must not silently alter tie behavior, because different ties can change placement quality across workloads. Validate that `logcnt`, ranks, and `log2phy` scatter indices remain identical in shape and range to the existing implementation. Do not script the current `heapq`/Python-list routine directly; replace only the hot fixed-shape kernel with script-compatible tensor control flow.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment as an exact assignment solver for targeted group-to-node repair around the current hierarchical layout
tried_paradigms.description: The hierarchy currently packs groups by their total load before it knows how much replication will later be needed inside each node. Consequently, a node can receive a mix whose aggregate group total looks balanced but whose concentrated hot experts consume many local replica slots and leave a worse achievable GPU makespan. Retain the current group ordering as a baseline, compute a per-group pressure score such as its predicted local bottleneck after the deterministic replica rule, and build a square cost matrix between group positions and node-specific group slots. The cost for placing group q into a node slot should include its pressure plus a deterministic penalty for moving it away from its original node, thereby allowing only beneficial cross-node changes. Call scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment once per layer to obtain a globally consistent reassignment of groups to node slots, then run the unchanged replication and local GPU packer. This differs from changing the GPU packer: it improves the upstream partition that determines which experts are even allowed to share replica capacity. It can be much faster than MILP because assignment is cubic in group count and has predictable runtime.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve hierarchical balance by reducing node-level hot-expert concentration before replica allocation; preserve or improve execution time relative to multi-swap local search or MILP.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Linear assignment optimizes additive placement costs, so the pressure score must be derived carefully from the actual replica-allocation bottleneck rather than raw group token sum alone. The current code requires each node to receive exactly groups_per_node contiguous logical-group slots; preserve this cardinality and reconstruct log2mlog/mlog2log consistently. If the evaluator penalizes movement or requires stable mappings across invocations, increase the movement penalty and deterministic tie breaking. Because the actual evaluator formula is absent from the shown wrapper, benchmark raw-load pressure, max-expert pressure, and predicted replica-load pressure rather than assuming one is correct.

tried_paradigms.description: The current hierarchy first assigns contiguous logical-expert groups to nodes using only each group's total token count, then replicates inside each node. This is strong because LPT equalizes raw node totals cheaply, but it ignores that a group containing one dominant expert benefits far more from the node's replica slots than a diffuse group with the same sum. Replace the group packing key with a replica-aware scalar computed directly from the group's sorted expert loads using torch.sort: estimate its post-replication bottleneck under the average physical-expert budget available per node. Pack groups in descending estimated bottleneck rather than descending group sum, while still using the existing cardinality-constrained heap assignment and preserving contiguous group structure. A practical estimate is the smallest threshold T for which sum over experts of ceil(load/T), clipped to the per-node physical capacity, predicts whether the group consumes disproportionate replica capacity; approximate this from the sorted prefix rather than solving an optimization problem. This changes the node decision to account for the downstream replication stage, which is the largest structural omission in the current program. Keep the existing global-policy fallback unchanged when hierarchy is disabled.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the eventual maximum per-GPU expert load by preventing highly skewed groups from being co-located merely because their total loads appear balanced; preserve low runtime with a per-group sort already small relative to later processing.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The adapter only exposes combined_score, not the original evaluator's metric breakdown, so validate this against both score and evaluator runtime rather than assuming sum-load balance is sufficient. Do not change group membership or violate equal groups-per-node capacity. Use float32/CPU consistently because the current function explicitly moves weights to CPU. The predictor must account for the fixed number of physical slots per node; otherwise it will overvalue replication that cannot actually be allocated.

tried_paradigms.description: Current balanced_packing performs LPT and examines exactly one swap between the single most-loaded and single least-loaded pack. That is extremely fast and explains its robustness, but it misses the common case where the final maximum is improved by exchanging with the second or third lightest/heaviest pack, or where the old minimum ceases to matter after a swap. After LPT, use heapq.nlargest to identify a tiny critical set of highest-load packs and lowest-load packs, for example two or three from each side, and evaluate all legal one-for-one swaps among only those packs. Select the swap with the best lexicographic sorted load vector: first minimize maximum pack load, then minimize the second maximum, then range. Apply only a strictly improving swap and repeat for a fixed very small number of passes, such as two, terminating early if no improvement exists. This is a local-search refinement rather than the previously failed assignment, MILP, or flow formulations: it preserves the actual equal-slot packing constraints and directly optimizes the load vector produced by the placement. It should be applied independently to both group-to-node packing and replica-to-GPU packing, where the latter is particularly sensitive to a single overloaded GPU.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly lower bottleneck node/GPU load and tail imbalance after LPT while retaining predictable bounded overhead, which should improve the balance component without materially harming runtime.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Compare the complete sorted vector or at least max then second-max, not only high-minus-low range: a swap can reduce range yet increase the maximum that likely drives service imbalance. Recompute loads for every candidate exactly and preserve per-pack cardinality and rank bookkeeping when accepted. Keep the critical set and pass count constant and small; exhaustive pack-pair local search can erase the current program's efficiency advantage. Avoid ties that churn placements without objective improvement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Batched water-filling replica allocation with torch.searchsorted
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts adds one replica at a time by repeatedly selecting argmax(weight/logcnt), which is the correct greedy water-filling principle for minimizing the largest isolated replica share, but it performs one full reduction per redundant physical expert and does not expose a direct threshold representation. For each layer/node, use torch.searchsorted over sorted candidate breakpoints load/k for k from 1 through the maximum possible replica count to find a common water level whose required replica counts sum to the physical-expert budget. Set each expert's replica count to ceil(load/level), clamped to at least one, then use a deterministic correction for any residual slots based on the next marginal load reduction. This produces the same or near-identical minimax allocation as sequential greedy but in a batched form, and makes it affordable to use the replica-aware group score proposed above. Because all replicas of an expert have equal load under the evaluator's presumed split model, this also gives a clean predicted physical load vector for the subsequent GPU LPT phase. Retain the existing rank construction after counts are decided, so the output maps and scatter-based inverse mapping remain valid. This targets efficiency first, but the exact threshold calculation can also remove float tie-order artifacts from repeated argmax decisions across layers.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce rebalance execution time in replication-heavy configurations and stabilize or improve the maximum per-replica load that feeds GPU packing, improving the combined score if evaluator runtime is included.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The original evaluator is not shown beyond its process wrapper, so first verify whether its combined score rewards runtime, balance, or both; do not trade a measurable balance loss for speed blindly. Handle zero-load experts, equality at breakpoints, and integer residual-slot correction deterministically so counts sum exactly to num_phy. Breakpoints must include all feasible k values up to the available redundant-slot budget, not merely a fixed small k, or highly hot experts will be under-replicated. This replaces only count selection; placement must still honor node boundaries and physical expert rank indexing.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 to make load-correlated expert groups before the existing hierarchy
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first partitions logical experts into fixed contiguous groups, and only then balances the summed group loads over nodes. This means a group containing several simultaneously hot experts is indivisible and can force node-level imbalance which replication inside that node cannot repair. Build one feature vector per logical expert from its normalized load across layers, then call scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 with k=num_groups to form equal-size-like load-diverse groups; use deterministic whitening/normalization so large-load layers do not dominate all others. Convert each cluster into a fixed-capacity group by deterministically spilling excess members to their nearest underfull cluster, then order the resulting groups as the logical group layout used by the existing hierarchical code. The existing group-to-node LPT, node-local replica allocation, and GPU packing can remain unchanged. This is structurally different from repairing a placement after packing: it removes correlated hot experts from the indivisible units that the hierarchy must place. It should especially help workloads where the same experts are hot in many layers, because their group sums become less skewed and node-local replication budget becomes more useful.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the node-level bottleneck created by fixed contiguous groups, thereby improving the evaluator's load-balance component without adding an expensive per-layer exact solver.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The output still must respect exactly group_size experts per group and preserve a bijection of logical expert IDs. Clustering must be deterministic by setting a fixed initialization/seed and should be skipped for tiny group sizes or when the current contiguous groups are already less imbalanced. Do not cluster independently per layer: the implementation's mapping layout is shared structurally and inconsistent grouping would complicate valid inverse maps. The evaluator wrapper shown does not expose the underlying score decomposition, so benchmark both balance and runtime rather than assuming a particular imbalance formula.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing as a direct bounded discrete search over bottleneck-node group exchanges
tried_paradigms.description: The present balanced_packing is LPT with only one swap between the currently highest and lowest pack. It misses improvements requiring an exchange involving a middle node, a two-pair cycle, or a temporarily non-improving move before the maximum node load decreases. For only the layers with materially large group-pack spread, formulate a direct objective over a small set of selected groups on overloaded and underloaded nodes: decode each continuous annealing coordinate into a deterministic integer swap/cycle choice, reject choices violating the exact groups_per_node capacity, and evaluate the actual maximum node load after the decoded permutation. Call scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once for this direct objective, seeded from the LPT layout but not as a separate assignment solver, and retain the candidate only if it improves the lexicographic objective of maximum load first and load range second. Limit the variable set to, for example, the few heaviest groups on the worst nodes plus the few lightest groups on candidate recipient nodes; all other groups remain fixed. After a better node assignment is found, run the existing replication and GPU packing unchanged. This targets the combinatorial blind spot of the one-extreme-swap heuristic rather than the MILP, assignment, and min-cost-flow formulations that previously showed no gain.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve worst-node load before replication, which is a hard topology constraint and can dominate any later GPU-level balancing; apply only on difficult layers to keep total execution time controlled.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a strict, small evaluation budget and a wall-clock guard, because the evaluator has a finite process timeout and Python objective callbacks are costly. The decoded state must always be a valid cardinality-preserving permutation, not a rounded arbitrary assignment. This is appropriate only for a targeted low-dimensional repair; applying it to every group and every layer will likely lose on runtime. Since it is stochastic by default, fix the RNG seed and use improvement-only acceptance for reproducible evaluator behavior.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use torch.scatter_reduce to replace Python-row LPT and enable a richer batched best-exchange pass
tried_paradigms.description: The current code moves weights to CPU, invokes sort(...).indices.tolist(), iterates through every layer and group in Python, and constructs Python heaps and nested swap loops. Those conversions and scalar loops can be a significant part of the measured algorithm cost, while restricting affordable refinement to one high-versus-low swap. Re-express LPT state for all layers as tensors: sort group weights once, maintain per-layer per-pack loads and occupancy masks, select the least-loaded available pack with tensor reductions, and update loads and assignments using torch.scatter_reduce/scatter operations. With the Python overhead removed, evaluate all valid exchanges between pack pairs in parallel and select the single best global improving exchange per layer, or repeat a very small fixed number of passes until no strict max-load improvement remains. The exchange criterion should recompute the full affected pack loads and accept only moves that improve the layer's maximum GPU/node load, with range as a tie-breaker; this avoids the current absolute two-bin-gap rule accepting a swap that is locally attractive but irrelevant to the global maximum. Apply this vectorized implementation to both group-to-node and physical-expert-to-GPU packing, retaining the exact map/rank semantics expected by the existing inverse and scatter construction. This is an efficiency-led improvement that can also improve balance by making broader local search cheap enough.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lower rearrangement execution time and use that budget for a globally valid multi-pack exchange refinement, improving final node/GPU maximum load rather than merely the range of one extreme pair.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Pack capacity must be included in the availability mask at every greedy assignment; selecting an already-full low-load pack creates invalid rank indices. Keep calculations in float32/float64 consistently with the existing float conversion and preserve deterministic tie-breaking by incorporating pack ID into ties. Tensorizing small instances can be slower than the existing heap, so retain a small-size fallback. Ensure accepted exchanges update both pack_index and rank_in_pack coherently; a correct load objective is insufficient if the returned placement no longer forms a permutation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replica-aware threshold-feasibility node packing using bisect.bisect_left
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first balances raw group token sums across nodes, then independently allocates a fixed number of replicas inside each node. This is mismatched to the eventual load because a node containing a very hot expert can reduce its effective load through replicas, whereas a node containing several moderately hot but non-replicable experts may remain a bottleneck. Replace the Step-1 LPT objective with a direct feasibility test for a candidate node peak T: for each prospective node, estimate the minimum replica counts needed for its assigned experts so that every expert share is at most T, namely ceil(weight/T), and reject assignments whose required counts exceed the node physical-expert budget. Binary-search the smallest feasible T with bisect.bisect_left over sorted candidate share loads, while greedily placing groups by decreasing required-replica pressure rather than raw group mass. The constructed node assignment should preserve exactly groups_per_node groups per node and should use the same existing replica-map output construction afterward. This attacks the hierarchy-induced replication bottleneck without invoking MILP, flow, assignment, or a post-hoc optimization stage. It is especially valuable when a small number of experts dominate load and the raw group sums hide their different replica demands.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The eventual maximum per-GPU/per-node expert load after replication, rather than the current proxy of pre-replication group token sum. This can improve the primary balance component while retaining the hierarchical topology constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The feasibility accounting must include the mandatory one copy of every logical expert and the fixed physical-expert count per node; summing ceil(weight/T) alone is insufficient unless zero-load experts are handled correctly. Candidate thresholds must use float-safe comparisons and a deterministic tie break. Do not run an expensive binary search over arbitrary floating values; search only a bounded sorted set of weight/k candidate values or use a small fixed number of iterations. If a group cannot be split, estimate its replica need as the sum of member requirements, not ceil of its total group sum.

tried_paradigms.idea: Incremental marginal-cost group placement with heapq.heapreplace
tried_paradigms.description: The existing LPT node packer scores each group only by its total raw load, which ignores the discontinuous reduction caused by allocating an additional replica to one of the group’s experts. Define a node-state score equal to the predicted post-replication bottleneck after assigning all of that node’s experts its fixed local physical slots using the same greedy max(weight/count) rule as replicate_experts. For each group, compute its marginal increase in this score if appended to every eligible node, then place it into the currently best eligible node while enforcing the exact groups_per_node cardinality. Maintain candidate node states incrementally with heapq.heapreplace rather than recomputing full packing or sorting all nodes after every group. Order groups by a dominance statistic such as maximum member weight, second maximum member weight, and total load, so groups with the least interchangeable hot experts are committed first. This is fundamentally different from the failed replica-aware ordering experiment because the decision criterion is the simulated final replicated peak of each destination, not merely a different sort order for raw groups. It also differs from flow and linear assignment formulations by directly modeling the integer replica-allocation discontinuities in the placement heuristic. After the node layout is chosen, retain the existing efficient greedy replica allocation and GPU LPT implementation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce node-level hotspots that persist after the fixed local replica budget is consumed, which is the principal weakness of independently optimizing raw group packing and later replication. Keep runtime near current heap-based complexity.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The marginal simulator must be cheap: maintain per-node expert weights/counts and update only the affected expert/group summary rather than cloning a full tensor for every candidate node. Group placement needs an eligibility rule for remaining group slots, otherwise greedy early choices can violate exact node capacity. Use deterministic ordering and stable expert-id tie breaks because small nondeterministic layout differences may affect evaluator consistency. Do not add a later exhaustive swap phase, since that duplicates the previously unsuccessful critical-bin exchange direction and can dominate runtime.

tried_paradigms.description: Reserve topology capacity for hot experts before conventional group balancing. Per layer, use numpy.partition to identify the upper tail of logical-expert weights whose ideal replica count exceeds one under the global average physical-expert budget. Build a lightweight reservation signature for every group: number of hot experts, their total excess replica demand, and the largest unsplit expert. Disperse these signatures across nodes with a round-robin or least-reserved-capacity rule before placing the remaining groups using the current LPT policy. The key structural benefit is preventing several independent replica-hungry experts from landing on the same node, where the fixed local replica count forces them to compete and leaves their per-replica shares high. Unlike changing the replica allocator, this changes only the topology partition and leaves the proven greedy allocator and physical-GPU packer intact. Unlike the failed torch.sort proposal, partition is used only to identify a small robust hot set, not to impose a full replica-aware ordering of all groups. The hot-tail threshold can be derived directly from num_physical_experts/num_logical_experts and therefore requires no evaluator-specific tuned hyperparameter.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Avoid catastrophic local replica-budget contention and improve tail/max-load balance, with low overhead because selection is linear-time rather than a full repeated sort or solver invocation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Reservation must still honor indivisible original groups; it cannot scatter experts that are already in the same group. For nearly uniform layers, the hot set should be empty or very small so that behavior falls back to the existing LPT scheme rather than injecting noise. Count only excess demand beyond the mandatory first copy, or low-load experts will incorrectly consume reservation capacity. Keep all calculations on the CPU float tensor already used by rebalance_experts and convert indices back to torch int64 tensors exactly as required by inverse and scatter operations.
